evidence.note: Every step carries an Analysis (current state) + Plan (next items) pair, functioning as a rolling prose ledger of near-term remaining work, giving a roughly accurate but frontier-only view rather than a persistent full-horizon checklist.
Enumerates a concrete batch of remaining items (bookmarks GET, status edit/history, admin role checks, session auth bug, /public, edit-profile UI) — checklist-style tracking of what's left.

Cross-checks seed-data requirements against exact spec numbers (22 statuses, 11 authors, 10 tags, 2 CW, 2 media) and then systematically probes admin scopes, introspection, and search — genuine spec cross-check and multi-subsystem coverage sweep for that area.

Repeated route-order/sed breakage recurs (search 404, notifications 404, broken decorators) without the agent naming the thrashing or switching away from the error-prone edit method — a stuck/circular pattern it does not detect.

Large parts of the constraint set (lists, polls, pagination, cache validators, SSE, CSP/purple-palette realism gate) never appear in any plan, so horizon-level coverage tracking is incomplete; no explicit implemented-vs-verified distinction and no visible final systematic constraint sweep.

reasoning: The agent keeps a usable, roughly accurate running view of remaining work through consistent Analysis/Plan pairs and does cross-check seed counts against the spec and spot-check several subsystems (admin, introspection, search, notifications, bookmarks) — matching the level-5 anchor. It falls short of level 8 because the tracking is frontier-only prose rather than an explicit ledger mapping every subsystem/constraint to a status, whole required areas (lists, polls, cache validators, realism gate) are never surfaced, and it does not recognize or name the recurring sed-induced file breakage as thrashing.
